title: Check-in schedule
summary: Each lesson comes back on its own period; passing spreads it out, failing brings it back tomorrow.
description: Every lesson comes back on its own schedule. The gap grows from the time that actually passed, so that remembering after longer is worth more.

stories.want: each lesson to come back when I am about to forget it
stories.soThat: I review what needs it and nothing else

requirements.text: A new lesson's period defaults by kind and complexity: drills 2, 4 and 7 days for low, medium and high; conversations 5, 7 and 10.
The learner can change a lesson's period on its page.
The first pass brings the lesson back after its period; a first ace, after three times its period.
Each later pass sets the next gap to the days since the last check-in times the lesson's ease, never less than its period and never less than the days that passed plus one.
Days since the last check-in count for at most twice the previous gap.
An ace raises the ease by 0.15 and grows the gap by a further 1.3 times.
A partial repeats the period and lowers the ease by 0.15.
A fail brings the lesson back the next day and lowers the ease by 0.2.
Ease starts at `ease.start` and stays between `ease.min` and `ease.max`.
The gap worked out for a check-in is never longer than `schedule.max-gap`; spreading can then place it up to a week later.
A check-in four days or more ahead is placed on the lightest day within a tenth of the gap either side of its target: at least one day and at most seven.
A lesson done before it is due is an early check-in: full XP, and its schedule moves.
Extra practice on a lesson already passed today does not move its schedule.

history.text: Extra practice on a lesson already passed today pays half XP and does not move its schedule.
history.reason: What extra practice pays is said once, in PROG-3; the schedule keeps only what it decides.

values.description: The longest gap worked out between two check-ins.
